title.en: Betzilo chimadti: the sukkah as the shade of emunah

summary.en: The Rav opens with the Zohar on 'betzilo chimadti veyashavti': a Jew longs to sit in the sukkah, the shade of emunah under the wings of the Shechinah. He brings that the sukkah carries the holiness of Eretz Yisrael and of the Beis HaMikdash, and reconciles the Midrash that reads the same passuk on the Beis HaMikdash.

title.en: Yaakov Avinu, root of the sukkah

summary.en: The Rav shows that the holiness of the sukkah comes from Yaakov Avinu, who made sukkos and to whom the Beis HaMikdash came in chutz la'aretz. He brings the Zohar that after his encounter with Esav Yaakov went to Sukkos, as Jews enter the sukkah after Yom Kippur, and the Zera Kodesh that the earthly sechach is a shadow of Hashem's heavenly sukkah.

title.en: Sukkos, the Yom Tov of bitachon

summary.en: The Rav explains that each Yom Tov has a segulah one takes for the whole year: Rosh Hashanah yiras Shamayim, Yom Kippur teshuvah, Pesach emunah, Shavuos Torah and Sukkos bitachon. He contrasts a fortified house with a flimsy sukkah that rain can enter, and brings the Ramban that bitachon is a level above emunah.

title.en: The sukkah as one's dwelling and rain on the first night

summary.en: The Rav brings the dispute of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Akiva on whether the sukkos were clouds of glory or actual huts, and the Bach's reason why the Tur and Shulchan Aruch follow Rabbi Eliezer. He then asks why the Rambam limits the bad sign of rain to the first night, and answers with the Divrei Chaim that the sukkah is one's address: the first meal establishes it, and later rain is only like a leak in the roof.

title.en: The Rokeach: sukkos in the war with Sichon and Og

summary.en: The Rav brings the Rokeach that Rabbi Akiva's 'actual sukkos' were the huts the Jews lived in during the war with Sichon and Og, and asks what that minor detail has to do with the miracle of the Exodus. He answers that both Tannaim agree the miracle was the protection of the clouds of glory; Rabbi Akiva adds that this protection went out with them to war, so instead of digging trenches they sat in flimsy sukkos.

title.en: Teivah, Mishkan and sukkah: holiness by measurement

summary.en: The Rav notes that the Torah gives measurements in three places: Noach's teivah, the Mishkan and the sukkah. Measurement belongs to the lowest level, and a lofty light can only be drawn into this world through it; the teivah lifted Noach out of the world under the decree, and so the sukkah's walls and sechach lift a Jew to where a harsh decree does not apply. He connects 'ki yitzpeneni besukko' to the teivah and explains why sleeping is central to dwelling in the sukkah.

title.en: Chizkiyahu's sleep: bitachon in the sukkah

summary.en: The Rav tells how Chizkiyahu went to sleep while Sanheriv's huge army besieged Yerushalayim, and that night the army was destroyed; his greatness was that he could sleep. From here he explains that one sits in the sukkah with calm and security so that one can sleep there, and that this bitachon is Yaakov Avinu's gift.

title.en: Lulav and esrog: bringing the sukkah's light inward

summary.en: The Rav brings from the Arizal that the light of the sukkah is a makif, too lofty to enter a person, and that taking the lulav and esrog in the sukkah and bringing them to the heart draws it inward. He connects this to Rabban Yochanan ben Zakai's enactment to take the lulav all seven days as a remembrance of the Mikdash, since the sukkah carries the Mikdash's holiness.

title.en: Yaakov's bitachon and protection for all generations

summary.en: The Rav brings pesukim showing that bitachon belongs to Yaakov and that the sukkah is Yaakov's inheritance to his children. According to Rabbi Akiva the sukkah's protection moves from place to place and so from time to time, for the whole year and all generations, as in Hashkiveinu. He describes the Jewish people surrounded by enemies, especially in Eretz Yisrael, kept safe by open miracles every day.

title.en: The sukkah protects the whole world; bitachon brings simcha

summary.en: The Rav explains that a Jew's mitzvos affect all of creation, as washing negel vasser removes impurity from the whole world, so a Jew who exerts himself for the mitzvah of sukkah may protect thousands in Eretz Yisrael. He then asks why Sukkos is the time of joy and answers that simcha comes from bitachon: one who knows Hashem is his insurance can rejoice.

title.en: Simcha and somech; atzvus and azuv

summary.en: The Rav brings the approach that similar-sounding words are related: simcha is linked to somech, having something firm to lean on, while atzvus comes from azuv, being forsaken. He then describes Yaakov as the middle bar that runs through all levels, and says that while there are lofty levels of bitachon, every Jew can climb gradually to some measure of it.

title.en: Bitachon in practice: davening, eyes and the telephone

summary.en: The Rav gives concrete applications of bitachon: not rushing davening for business but davening with a minyan that davens with chayus even if it means arriving later; not being curious in the street; and not interrupting a learning seder or a seudah for a telephone call that might bring business. He brings the Be'er Mayim Chaim on one who runs after parnassah.

title.en: The sukkah as Eretz Yisrael: judgment reopened

summary.en: The Rav notes that the Gemara puts the sealing of judgment on Yom Kippur, while the Zohar extends it to Shemini Atzeres and sefarim in the name of the Arizal until Chanukah. He explains this with the Gemara in Makkos that one who flees to Eretz Yisrael has his judgment reopened in its merit: entering the sukkah is entering Eretz Yisrael and the Mikdash, so the judgment is heard anew.

title.en: Zman simchaseinu: ruach hakodesh, chassadim and joy

summary.en: The Rav closes that on Sukkos one draws emunah, bitachon and ruach hakodesh, which he explains with the Divrei Chaim as being aimed at the truth of Torah. He calls for taking simcha and bitachon for the whole year, davening with a minyan that davens with feeling, and brings from the Arizal that Sukkos draws chassadim that sweeten the judgments, ending with a tefillah that Hashem rejoice with His people.

catalogTitle: Waiting for Miriam in the Desert and the Hidden Treasure of ט' באב

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains why the Jews' waiting for Miriam, which made the meraglim return on Tisha B'Av, was in the end a reward: Tisha B'Av is a 'mo'ed' with a hidden good root, the day Mashiach is born.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the passuk that the people did not travel until Miriam returned, and brings the Satmar Rav: because of those seven days the meraglim came back on Tisha B'Av, an ill-fated day. He traces a chain of lashon hara from Miriam to the meraglim to both churbanos, and sees the recent movement for guarding one's speech as a sign of the Geulah. He then asks why Miriam, a tzadeikes, should be the cause, and compares Moshe's added day at Sinai that led to the luchos breaking on Shiva Asar B'Tammuz. Turning to the inner side of Tisha B'Av, he calls it a mo'ed that went sour, which will become the greatest yom tov, the day Mashiach is born. Days, like people, have tzaddikim and reshaim, and a hidden root. He concludes that waiting for Miriam placed the meraglim's sin on Tisha B'Av, whose hidden good gave them hope of tikkun.

en: According to the Satmar Rav, the seven days the people waited for Miriam made the meraglim return on Tisha B'Av instead of seven days earlier.
The Rav traces a chain of lashon hara from Miriam through the meraglim to the first and second churban.
Tisha B'Av is called a mo'ed because it has a good inner side; when Mashiach comes it will be the greatest yom tov.
Just as there are tzaddikim and reshaim among people, there are tzaddik days and rasha days in the calendar, and a rasha's teshuvah transforms his day too.
Hidden within Tisha B'Av is the third Beis HaMikdash, and from Tisha B'Av one draws for the whole year the knowledge that every tzarah hides good.
Because they waited for Miriam, the meraglim's sin fell on the day of the birth of Mashiach ben David, whose good point gave them hope; so the waiting was a reward for Miriam.

birth of Mashiach on Tisha B'Av
the hidden root in every Jew

title.en: Waiting for Miriam led to Tisha B'Av

summary.en: The Rav opens with the passuk that the people did not travel until Miriam returned, a reward for her waiting for Moshe. He brings the Satmar Rav that without those seven days the meraglim would have returned before Tisha B'Av, an ill-fated day, and perhaps there would have been no Tisha B'Av at all.

title.en: Hashem's plan and the chain of lashon hara

summary.en: The Rav explains that Hashem's plans come about through causes, answers a listener's question on free will with the Rambam, and traces lashon hara from Miriam to the meraglim to both churbanos. He sees the recent movement to learn the laws of lashon hara, begun by the Chafetz Chaim, as Hashem sending agents to repair this flaw before the Geulah.

title.en: Why Miriam? Moshe's added day at Sinai

summary.en: The Rav asks why Miriam, a tzadeikes whose song is eternal, should cause the churban, and whether she would not rather have stayed in the desert. He brings a similar question from a sefer: Moshe's added day at Sinai made the forty days end on Shiva Asar B'Tammuz, so the luchos were broken, connected to the Magen Avraham's question on the date of Shavuos.

title.en: Tisha B'Av, a mo'ed that went sour

summary.en: The Rav explains that Tisha B'Av is called a mo'ed and has a good inner side. He describes levels of talmidei chachamim like Shabbos, Yom Tov and Chol HaMoed, and compares Tisha B'Av to a gifted bochur who went sour but can be brought back and become great. The 22 days from Shiva Asar B'Tammuz to Tisha B'Av correspond to the 22 holiest days of Tishrei.

title.en: Torah of the Nine Days and kiddush for Tisha B'Av

summary.en: The Rav tells of a sefer by a tzaddik, the grandfather of the Bluzhever Rebbe, whose greatest Torah for Sukkos was prepared during the Nine Days. He then tells of a great tzaddik who, on Shabbos Chazon, lifted a cup of wine and made kiddush for Tisha B'Av, as a picture of the days of Mashiach, with tears streaming from his eyes.

title.en: The ascent to Shavuos and the descent after

summary.en: The Rav describes the yearly climb from Chamisha Asar B'Shvat through Purim and Pesach to the peak of Shavuos, and the descent that begins after it. He mentions Chaf Sivan, a fast day for the massacres of the Crusades, later persecutions and the Holocaust deportations, as part of the slide toward Tisha B'Av.

title.en: Mashiach's birthday and days that are reshaim

summary.en: The Rav brings the Midrash that on Tisha B'Av a soul with the potential of Mashiach is born, which explains customs of rising from the floor. He brings the Chasam Sofer that Pesach was once a fast day for Avraham and was transformed, as Tisha B'Av will be. Days, like people, are tzaddikim and reshaim; a rasha is rooted in Tisha B'Av, and his teshuvah transforms his day too.

title.en: The hidden root and the hidden Beis HaMikdash

summary.en: The Rav says the galus is needed like the Geulah, and that even the greatest rasha has a hidden good point, the root represented by Yom Kippur, the fortieth day, like the fortieth lash that is not given. He brings Tosafos in Chagigah on the 'hidden' gematria of the letters, and applies it to Tisha B'Av: what is hidden in it is the third Beis HaMikdash.

title.en: What we draw from Tisha B'Av; Miriam's reward

summary.en: The Rav says each yom tov feeds the whole year, and from Tisha B'Av one draws the knowledge that every tzarah hides good. He concludes that the meraglim had a hidden root, and because they waited for Miriam their sin fell on Tisha B'Av, the day of Mashiach's birth, whose good point gave them hope, so the waiting was a reward for Miriam.

catalogTitle: דברי כיבושין לפני פסד"ז: תשנ"ח- דוד אושפיזא דיומא הורה תשובה ליחיד (ניגונים מהלל)

oneLiner.en: Bringing the Imrei Emes, the Rav explains that Hoshana Rabbah, the day of Dovid HaMelech, is a great salvation even for the individual Jew whom Yom Kippur could not help, through enlisting in Dovid's army of tefillah.

abstract.en: Speaking before Pesukei d'Zimra on Hoshana Rabbah, the Rav brings the Imrei Emes that Hoshana Rabbah is a great salvation, greater than Yom Kippur. Yom Kippur atones for the golden calf, which taught teshuvah for the many; Hoshana Rabbah belongs to Dovid HaMelech, whose sin taught teshuvah for the individual, the Jew with a barrier who could not join the klal. So the Hoshana Rabbah aravah is taken apart from the lulav. The days of Sukkos are days of war against the seventy nations, the four species are the weapons, and the chief one is the aravah, the lips: tefillah, Dovid's strength. Through Magen Avraham and Magen Dovid, and Dovid's men in distress, the Rav concludes that every Jew can enlist in Dovid's army and will come to his tikkun.

en: According to the Imrei Emes, Hoshana Rabbah is a great salvation that can help even those whom Yom Kippur did not help.
Yom Kippur, the atonement of the golden calf, is teshuvah for the many; Hoshana Rabbah, connected to Dovid HaMelech, is teshuvah for the individual.
The aravah of Hoshana Rabbah is taken by itself, not with the lulav bundle, for Jews who had a barrier and could not join the klal.
The days of Sukkos are days of war against the seventy nations, the four species are the weapons, and the chief weapon is the aravah, the lips, which is tefillah.
On Hoshana Rabbah, the day of Dovid HaMelech as ushpiza, a Jew enlists in Dovid's army, whose strength is tefillah.
Every Jew has a hidden point of emunah from Avraham and a point of tefillah from Dovid, which Hashem guards, so that even the lowest can come to his tikkun.

title.en: Teshuvah for the individual

summary.en: The Rav brings the Imrei Emes that Hoshana Rabbah is a great salvation, greater than Yom Kippur. He explains with the Gemara on the golden calf (teshuvah for the many) and Dovid (teshuvah for the individual), and why the aravah of Hoshana Rabbah is taken apart from the lulav.

title.en: Enlisting in Dovid HaMelech's army

summary.en: The Rav connects the beaten hoshana to 'mekimi me'afar dal', then explains that the days of Sukkos are days of war against the seventy nations with the four species as weapons. On Dovid's day one enlists in his army, whose main weapon is the aravah, the lips: tefillah.

title.en: The aravah's longing and the point of tefillah

summary.en: The Rav explains that the aravah, with no taste and no smell, stands for Jews who have nothing but long to be good, and brings the Zohar on the power of words of longing; Hoshana Rabbah was made for them, with Dovid as their shliach tzibbur. He then brings the idea of Magen Avraham guarding every Jew's point of emunah, and the Imrei Emes's addition that Magen Dovid guards the point of tefillah.

title.en: Dovid's men and the promise of tikkun

summary.en: From the men in distress, in debt and bitter of soul who joined Dovid, the Rav shows that even Jews who cannot mend their deeds can enlist with Dovid and come to tikkun. He speaks of the weapons of Dovid's army, chiefly tefillah, and closes with a brachah for a great salvation together with all Jews.

catalogTitle: דברי כיבושין לפני פסד"ז: תש"ס - להקים את סוכת דוד הנופלת!

oneLiner.en: The Rav reads the passuk of the evyon in tomorrow's Torah reading as a hint to Moshiach, who longs for Klal Yisrael, and calls on everyone to bind himself to Dovid HaMelech on his ushpizin day so as to raise up the fallen sukkah of Dovid.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the passuk in tomorrow's reading, 'ki yihyeh vecha evyon me'achad achecha be'achad she'arecha', and brings a remez that the evyon is Moshiach, who is called 'poor and riding on a donkey'. He is poor because he lacks us: he longs to redeem Klal Yisrael, as in the Midrash where Moshiach weeps on hearing from Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi that the Jews await him. 'Achad she'arecha' hints that if one kehillah, one shul, did teshuvah, Ben Dovid would come at once; since great kehillos of earlier generations did not bring him, the Rav says it refers to a humble kehillah of ikvesa diMeshicha in today's hester panim. Hence no one may harden his heart to Moshiach's longing. Today is the ushpizin of Dovid, whose name is mentioned in Pesukei Dezimra and Hallel; Hashem's sukkah, Yerushalayim, fell with the churban, and the Rav asks that, bound to Dovid, we merit to raise the fallen sukkah of Dovid.

en: The Rav brings a remez that the 'evyon' of the passuk is Moshiach, who is poor because he lacks Klal Yisrael and longs to redeem them.
'Be'achad she'arecha' hints that the teshuvah of one single kehillah or shul would bring Ben Dovid at once.

Since great kehillos over almost two thousand years did not bring Moshiach, the Rav concludes the passuk refers to a humble kehillah of ikvesa diMeshicha, whose every movement toward Hashem in today's hester panim is as precious as the great avodos of earlier generations.
Today is the ushpizin of Dovid HaMelech, who has a great aliyah, and when Jews say his songs in Pesukei Dezimra and Hallel he is, as it were, saying them with us and will plead for us.
Hashem made Himself a sukkah in the world, Yerushalayim, which Dovid and Shlomo strengthened and which fell at the churban, becoming the 'fallen sukkah of Dovid' that we ask today to raise up.

title.en: Moshiach as the evyon who longs for us

summary.en: The Rav reads the passuk of the evyon in tomorrow's reading as a remez to Moshiach, who lacks and longs for Klal Yisrael, and explains 'achad she'arecha' as the one humble kehillah of the last generation whose teshuvah would bring Ben Dovid. He concludes that no one may harden his heart to the longing of Moshiach and the Shechinah.

title.en: Dovid's ushpizin and the fallen sukkah

summary.en: The Rav explains that today is the ushpizin of Dovid HaMelech, whose songs Jews say in Pesukei Dezimra and Hallel, and brings the Midrash that Hashem's sukkah in the world is Yerushalayim, which fell at the churban. He calls on everyone to bind himself to Dovid and closes with a tefillah to raise up the fallen sukkah of Dovid.

catalogTitle: דברי כיבושין לפני פסד"ז: תשס"ב- אונז פירן מלחמה ע"י תורה ותפילה!

oneLiner.en: On Hoshana Rabbah, with a war having broken out that very night, the Rav tells the bochurim that the war of Gog uMagog is fought by Jews with Torah, tefillah and good middos, and calls them to strengthen their davening over the three great days and the coming year.

abstract.en: The Rav recalls that the previous day he spoke of the war of Gog uMagog, which is said to begin on Hoshana Rabbah, and explains why he addresses the bochurim in particular: the years of youth are worth more, and great Rebbes invested in young people. He then notes that the new war broke out exactly as Hoshana Rabbah began, and that its fighters said the moon helped them; from the Ramban on the shadow that departed from the meraglim and from the stars that fought for Devorah, he concludes that the moon has a share in this war and it may be Gog uMagog. The Jews are the real soldiers: with Tehillim, the four minim, Torah and tefillah they circle Yericho. He urges stronger davening, describes the greatness of Shemini Atzeres and the three books in which each Jew writes himself, and reads a letter of the Ba'al HaTanya on loud, unified davening.

en: The Rav says that if this is the war of Gog uMagog, the Jews must know they are its soldiers, fighting with Tehillim, the four minim, Torah and tefillah.
Jews have the power to overturn decrees, so the war of Gog uMagog need not come with all the frightening things described in the pesukim and midrashim.
The Rav says davening has weakened lately, and asks that people come on time and daven with warmth, since one good tefillah, blatt Gemara or kapitel Tehillim can save hundreds of Jews.
Shemini Atzeres is described as the greatest day of the year, when Hashem is alone with the Jews, and all the other Yamim Tovim are a preparation for it.
The three books opened on the Day of Judgment are empty; each Jew writes himself into one of them, but writing in is not enough without the signature of real commitment.
From a letter of the Ba'al HaTanya the Rav teaches that the congregation should daven together word by word in a raised voice, neither too long nor too short.

title.en: Why the Rav speaks to the bochurim

summary.en: The Rav recalls the previous day's talk about Gog uMagog, said to begin on Hoshana Rabbah, and the feeling of an emergency. He explains why he addresses the bochurim rather than the fathers: the years of youth are worth more, and the Gerer Rebbe and Rabbi Ben Zion of Bobov invested in young people.

title.en: The war that began on Hoshana Rabbah

summary.en: The Rav notes that the new war broke out just as Hoshana Rabbah began and that its fighters reported the moon helped them. From the Rema on the shadow on Hoshana Rabbah night, the Ramban on 'sar tzilam', and the stars that fought for Devorah, he concludes that this may be Gog uMagog, and that the Jews are its soldiers who circle Yericho with their tefillos.

title.en: Overturning the decree: our weapons

summary.en: The Rav says the haftaros of Sukkos and the midrashim describe Gog uMagog in frightening terms, but Jews can overturn decrees; he brings the Gemara on Chizkiyahu, who could have been Moshiach had he sung shirah. He cites the Ba'al Shem Tov that davening with kavanah on the three coming days is a segulah for the whole year, and names the Jewish weapons: Hashem's Name, the four minim, Torah, tefillah, good middos and yiras Shamayim.

title.en: Reminders, the power of youth, and weakened davening

summary.en: Like the Mesilas Yesharim, the Rav says he comes only to refresh what is known. He tells the bochurim their avodah is very precious in Heaven, says davening has weakened, and asks them to daven for the Jews in Eretz Yisroel and the soldiers. He describes the joy of Shemini Atzeres and Simchas Torah and the tradition of the malach Michael's torn shoes.

title.en: Shemini Atzeres and the three books

summary.en: The Rav describes Shemini Atzeres as the greatest day of the year, above nature, when Hashem is alone with the Jews. He brings the Toldos Yaakov Yosef that the three books opened on the Day of Judgment are empty and each Jew writes himself in, and compares writing in without commitment to a check left unsigned; he asks for a year of hasmadah, kavanah and good middos.

title.en: The Ba'al HaTanya's letter on davening together

summary.en: The Rav reads a letter of the Ba'al HaTanya asking his chassidim to daven together word by word in a raised voice, neither too long nor too short, with those who daven aloud standing around the chazzan, and he tells the bochurim this is their responsibility. He adds that Torah and tefillah strengthen each other, that Simchas Torah joy must come with yiras Shamayim and not wildness, and closes with wishes for a good year.

catalogTitle: The Jewish Connection to Eretz Yisroel

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that Adam's body was taken from the earth of Eretz Yisrael beneath the Mizbeach, so every Jew is drawn to the land as to his source, and the sin of the spies was unfaithfulness to that source, atoned for by the mitzvos of nesachim and challah.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the two senders of the spies: Hashem and the people, whose impure motives tainted the mission, and warns that every Jew is Hashem's messenger. He notes that the parshiyos of nesachim and challah follow the spies, and turns to the creation of Adam from the earth and of Chava from Adam. Adam's earth came from all of Eretz Yisrael and chiefly from the place of the Mizbeach; the cavity beneath it, where the wine of nesachim flows down, is the hole from which Hashem plucked Adam, the 'challah of the world'. From the law that everything is drawn back to its source he explains gravity, marriage as a reunion, love of one's homeland, and the bond of every Jew to Eretz Yisrael. The spies' sin was unfaithfulness to that source, like a divorce, and nesachim and challah were given as consolation and atonement.

en: The spies failed because they went as messengers of the people, whose trust in Hashem was not wholesome, rather than as messengers of Hashem.
Adam's earth was gathered from all of Eretz Yisrael, and its most important part, his brain and heart, from the place of the Mizbeach in Yerushalayim.
There is a law in creation that everything is drawn back to its source: the body to the earth, the soul to Heaven, a man to his wife, and a Jew to Eretz Yisrael.
The sin of the spies was that something insulated them from their source, so they found fault with the land they should have loved.
The parshiyos of nesachim and challah that follow the spies were given as consolation and as atonement for being unfaithful to the place of their origin.

title.en: Two senders of the spies

summary.en: The Rav explains that the spies had two senders, Hashem and the people, and that the people's impure motives brought evil into the mission. He warns that every Jew is a messenger of Hashem from the heavenly throne, then recounts the spies' bad report and the bitter sentence of forty years in the desert.

title.en: Nesachim and challah after the spies

summary.en: The Rav points out that right after the spies come the parshiyos of nesachim, the wine poured on the Mizbeach down through pipes to the depths, and of challah. He brings Rashi that this was good tidings that they would yet enter the land, and explains the mitzvah of separating challah for the kohen.

title.en: Adam from the earth, Chava from Adam

summary.en: For insight into challah the Rav turns to the creation of Adam and Chava: unlike all other creatures, Adam was created alone and Chava was built from his rib, so she is 'bone of my bones' and named Isha from Ish. He describes Adam's creation in two phases, first from the earth and then Chava from him.

title.en: Adam's earth from the Mizbeach

summary.en: The Rav asks why only Shabbos bread is called challah and recalls that Chava gave Adam the forbidden fruit on Friday. He then explains that Adam's earth was taken from the place of the Mizbeach, the 'place of his atonement', bringing the Gemara, the Targum Yonasan and the Midrash that the dust came from all over Eretz Yisrael.

title.en: The shisin cavity under the Mizbeach

summary.en: The Rav describes the shisin, the cavity beneath the Mizbeach into which the wine flows, and the rock from which the world was founded, which David HaMelech dug down to the depths. He brings Rabbi Yisroel's insight that this cavity is the place from which Hashem plucked out Adam's earth and formed him like a cake.

title.en: Adam, the challah and candle of the world

summary.en: The Rav explains that Adam is the challah of the world, and since Chava brought death upon him on Friday, women separate challah on Friday as atonement, which is why Shabbos bread is called challah. He cites the Rema on baking for Shabbos, and adds that Adam was also the candle of the world, so women light candles before Shabbos.

title.en: Everything returns to its source

summary.en: The Rav explains that Chava is the challah taken from Adam as Adam was taken from the earth, and states a law of nature that everything is attracted back to its source, which is the reason behind gravity and behind death. Man and woman were once one in Adam, partners are announced forty days before birth, and a marriage is a reunion.

title.en: Every Jew belongs to Eretz Yisrael

summary.en: The Rav explains that since Adam came from Eretz Yisrael, every Jewish body must return there, that only Yisrael are called Adam in terms of holiness, and that every nation loves the land it originates from. He brings Rashi that the dead will roll through tunnels to Eretz Yisrael to rise there, like plants that grow only in their own soil.

title.en: Livelihood, a wife and attraction

summary.en: Answering a question about choosing between two jobs, the Rav brings a published letter of the Satmar Rav that each person is drawn to what is his, and explains that a livelihood is a shidduch like a wife. He shows the attraction of mashpia and mekabel throughout nature and explains why the bond to a wife is stronger than to one's parents.

title.en: Insulated from the source: the spies

summary.en: The Rav calls Eretz Yisrael 'Mother Zion' and says every Jew should feel drawn to it, unless something insulates him, like rust between two wires. That is what happened to the spies, who went on others' errand and despised the land; he connects this to the sotah tested with dust of the Mikdash and to the Mizbeach weeping at a divorce.

title.en: Gittin: divorce and exile

summary.en: Using the rule that a first mention contains everything, the Rav asks why Gittin opens with a get brought from overseas to Eretz Yisrael, and answers that a man's land and wife are one source, so being cut off from both is one punishment. The spies preferred the desert to their origin, and the Gemara of the Churban is in Gittin because exile is a divorce from Eretz Yisrael.

title.en: Nesachim and challah as atonement

summary.en: The Rav brings the Ramban and Rashi that nesachim was given as consolation to the Jews in the desert, and explains that wine, which gladdens the heart, poured into the very cavity from which Adam was taken, atones for the spies' unfaithfulness to their source, as does its twin, the mitzvah of challah. He concludes that learning this sedra removes the rust that insulates a Jew from his Creator and from Eretz Yisrael.

catalogTitle: דברי כיבושין לפני פסד"ז: תשס"א - "וחרב פיפיות בידם"

oneLiner.en: On Hoshana Rabbah, the day of the war of Gog and Magog and of the aravah, the Rav teaches that the true battlefield is the shul, and that the 'double-edged sword' of the Jewish people is tefillah, the power of Dovid HaMelech.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the seventy bullocks of Sukkos, which correspond to the seventy nations, and explains that on Hoshana Rabbah all seventy are finished; Jews hold that this is the day of the war of Gog and Magog. It is the day of Dovid HaMelech and of malchus, whose power is tefillah, and the day of the aravah, which stands for the present generation that has neither taste nor smell, yet whose prayers Hashem does not despise. Turning to the war then raging in Eretz Yisrael, he says the real battlefield is the shul: the prayers of Jews are the 'double-edged sword', pesukei dezimra cut down the klipos, and the hakafos bring down the walls as at Yericho. From the na'arah who is blamed for not crying out, he teaches that Hashem will ask why we did not cry 'Hoshana'. He closes by calling every Jew a soldier and praying for the kingship of Hashem.

en: The seventy bullocks of Sukkos subdue the seventy nations day by day, and on Hoshana Rabbah all seventy are completed; this is the war of Gog and Magog.
Hoshana Rabbah is the day of Dovid HaMelech and of malchus, and the power of Dovid is tefillah.
The aravah, without taste or smell, is the present generation, yet Hashem does not despise its prayers.
The real battlefield of the war in Eretz Yisrael is the shul, and what the news reports is only a reflection of what was fought there.
Tefillah is the 'double-edged sword' of the Jewish people, and the Rav says it must be taken along for the whole year.
Like the na'arah who is blamed for not crying out, a Jew will be asked why he did not cry 'Hoshana'.

title.en: Seventy nations, Dovid and the aravah

summary.en: The Rav explains that the seventy bullocks of Sukkos subdue the seventy nations and are completed on Hoshana Rabbah, the day of the war of Gog and Magog and of Dovid's kingship. Dovid's power is tefillah, and the aravah, without taste or smell, is today's generation, whose prayer Hashem does not despise.

title.en: The shul is the battlefield

summary.en: Speaking of the war in Eretz Yisrael, the Rav says the true battlefield is the shul, where prayer, the power of Dovid, is the 'double-edged sword'. Pesukei dezimra cut down the klipos, the na'anuim and hakafos are weapons, and this tefillah must be taken along for the whole year.

title.en: Why did you not cry out?

summary.en: From the na'arah who is liable because she did not cry out, the Rav teaches that Hoshana Rabbah is the day of crying out, and that every Jew can at least cry 'Hoshana'. When Jews say Dovid's songs with intent, Dovid davens with them; he ends with a plea of mercy for Yerushalayim and Eretz Yisrael.

title.en: Every Jew a soldier; the day of malchus

summary.en: Bringing Devorah's words about those who did not come to help Hashem, the Rav says every Jew is a soldier who can say Tehillim and cry 'Hoshana'. Hoshana Rabbah is the day of malchus; he brings the Yismach Moshe on Dovid asking when he will be king, and closes with tefillah as the service of the heart.

catalogTitle: דברי כיבושין לפני פסד"ז: תשס"ו - הצעקה של המים התחתונים: "אנן בעינן למיהוי קמי מלכא!"

oneLiner.en: The Rav teaches that on Hoshana Rabbah, the day of the aravah and of Dovid HaMelech, a Jew who feels he is empty and has earned nothing receives from the treasury of free gifts, and his very lowliness becomes his tefillah.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the aravah, which has neither taste nor smell: today every Jew must feel the lowliness of his generation and of himself. Dovid made himself poor; this is the middah of malchus, which has nothing of its own. In the Midrash, Moshe was shown the treasuries of the mitzvos and the largest was the treasury of free gifts; it opens only for one who feels he has earned nothing, and it opens on Hoshana Rabbah, Dovid's day. A Jew who comes before Hashem as an empty aravah receives a spark of Dovid's soul. Dovid said 'va'ani tefillah', I am the tefillah, which the Rav explains with a mashal from Rabbi Yechezkel of Kuzmir about a poor man whose appearance is his request. Hoshana Rabbah's higher teshuvah prepares for Shemini Atzeres, the point of the whole year, and the Rav closes asking to say Dovid's songs with bitul.

en: The aravah, which has neither taste nor smell, teaches that on Hoshana Rabbah every Jew must feel the lowliness of his generation and of himself.
Dovid's middah, malchus, is to have nothing of one's own; Dovid was king and still felt himself the lowest of the low.
The treasury of free gifts, the greatest of all, opens only for a Jew who feels he has earned nothing and has no claim on Hashem, and it opens on Hoshana Rabbah.
A Jew who connects to Dovid's middah by begging Hashem as an empty aravah receives a spark of Dovid HaMelech's soul.
Dovid was the essence of tefillah: 'va'ani tefillah', his very state cried out to Hashem without explanation.
The teshuvah of Hoshana Rabbah, higher than that of Yom Kippur, is the preparation for Shemini Atzeres, the central point of the whole year.

title.en: The aravah, Dovid's lowliness and the treasury of free gifts

summary.en: The Rav opens with the aravah, without taste or smell, and Dovid's middah of malchus, having nothing of one's own. He brings the Midrash of the treasury of free gifts shown to Moshe, asks why not everyone receives from it, and answers that it opens only for one who feels he earned nothing; such a Jew receives a spark of Dovid's soul.

title.en: 'Va'ani tefillah': I myself am the tefillah

summary.en: The Rav explains Dovid's words 'va'ani tefillah' with a mashal from Rabbi Yechezkel of Kuzmir: a poor man in torn clothes need not explain, his appearance is his request. He contrasts the tearful avodah of earlier simple Jews with the lowly state of today's generation, which is itself its tefillah, and brings that Hashem kisses Jewish tefillos on this day of the lips.

title.en: Higher teshuvah toward Shemini Atzeres

summary.en: The Rav explains that as Yom Kippur prepares for Sukkos, Hoshana Rabbah's higher teshuvah prepares for Shemini Atzeres, which all the Yamim Tovim surround as their center point. He closes asking to say Dovid's songs in Pesukei Dezimra with bitul, to merit to be before the King and to rejoice with Dovid and Moshiach.

catalogTitle: דברי כיבושין לפני פסד"ז: תשס"ז - אנו בחיל של דוד המלך במלחמה כנגד משחיתי אמונה

oneLiner.en: On Hoshana Rabbah the Rav calls on every Jew, pressed and in debt to Hashem, to join the army of Dovid HaMelech in the spiritual war of Gog and Magog against emunah, through crying out, lowliness and tefillah.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the tradition that the war of Gog and Magog will be on Sukkos, its core on Hoshana Rabbah. Besides the physical war that will come with Mashiach, there is a spiritual war against emunah and the Torah, fought by the angelic ministers of the seventy nations, and it is already raging. Dovid HaMelech, today's guest, is the one who fights Hashem's wars; the arba minim are the weapons and the hakafos are the circling of Yericho, whose wall is the yetzer hara. Dovid's army was made of men who were pressed, in debt and bitter of soul, and the Rav says every Jew today fits that description and should gather around Dovid and sing his tefillos. Today one must cry out; the aravah, without taste or smell, shows that the chasimah comes through lowliness, not merits. He ends by calling to take on tefillah for the whole year.

en: The Rav says the spiritual war of Gog and Magog, against emunah, the Torah and its transmission to the next generation, has already begun, and its peak is on Hoshana Rabbah.
Dovid HaMelech, the guest of Hoshana Rabbah, leads this war, and the arba minim and the hakafos are its weapons, like the circling of Yericho whose wall is the yetzer hara.
Every Jew today is pressed, bitter of soul and in debt to Hashem, so he has the marks of Dovid's army and should join it.
Having nothing to pay the debt with, the Jew pays by crying out to Hashem on Hoshana Rabbah.
The chasimah of Hoshana Rabbah comes when the aravos are beaten on the ground, because Hashem looks at our lowliness rather than our merits.
Hoshana Rabbah is the day of tefillah, Dovid's trait, and the Rav calls to accept on oneself never to be without tefillah.

walls of Yericho and the yetzer hara

title.en: The spiritual war of Gog and Magog

summary.en: The Rav brings the tradition that the war of Gog and Magog is on Sukkos, its core on Hoshana Rabbah, and distinguishes a future physical war from a spiritual war against emunah that has already begun. He reads 'Lamah ragshu goyim' as the nations' ministers rising to tear Jews away from the Torah of Sinai.

title.en: Dovid's army and the walls of Yericho

summary.en: Hoshana Rabbah completes the seventy bulls brought for the nations, and Dovid HaMelech, its guest, fights Hashem's wars. The Rav compares the hakafos with the arba minim to the circling of Yericho, whose wall is the yetzer hara, and describes from the passuk the pressed, indebted and bitter men who gathered to Dovid.

title.en: We are Dovid's soldiers: crying out

summary.en: The Rav says every Jew today has the signs of Dovid's army and should gather around him and sing his tefillos. Lacking anything to pay his debt, he must cry out; he brings the Chiddushei HaRim on the betrothed girl who cried out, and the aravah without taste or smell, held while setting aside every merit.

title.en: Lowliness, lips and tefillah

summary.en: Citing the Arizal, the Rav says the chasimah comes when the aravos are beaten, since Hashem looks at lowliness, not merits. From the Zohar on 'im tishkevun bein shefatayim' he explains the aravah as the lips, and ends calling to take on tefillah, Dovid's trait and the day's essence, with brachos for a good sealing.

catalogTitle: The Transformation of the קללות of בלעם and the Bitterness of תמוז

oneLiner.en: The Rav shows how Parshas Balak, read before Shiva Asar B'Tammuz, carries the seed of Mashiach, and how the month of Tammuz, which lost its place like Reuven, will be transformed from bitterness to the highest joy.

abstract.en: The Rav reads the Rambam's uncensored halachos of Mashiach, stressing that one must not only believe in Mashiach but long for him, and that Bilaam's prophecy in Balak foretells him. Since Shabbos holds the blessings of the coming week, Shabbos Balak carries the potential for the three weeks from Shiva Asar B'Tammuz to become days of joy. He explains why Tammuz is a month of strict judgment, linking it to Korach's machlokes. Following the Arizal, Korach meant well: he sought the world of tikkun, where the Leviim will be Kohanim. Dasan and Aviram, from Reuven, sought the return of the firstborn's priesthood. Tammuz corresponds to Reuven, who fell from first to fourth, so Tammuz fell too. Against the Ohr HaChaim, the Rema MiPano gives Dasan and Aviram a tikkun, which means Tammuz will be rectified. Balak himself held the seed of Mashiach, and Yiftach, the rejected 'Tammuz soul', holds the keys to the redemption.

en: According to the Rambam as the Rav reads him, belief in Mashiach includes longing for his coming; one who is not eager for it does not truly believe.
Shabbos Balak holds the blessing of the week of Shiva Asar B'Tammuz: the potential for the three weeks to become days of Mashiach's coming.
Korach, and in part Dasan and Aviram, argued in order to bring the world of tikkun at once, where the Leviim and the firstborn will again be the Kohanim.
Tammuz corresponds to Reuven: as Reuven fell from first to fourth through his sin, Tammuz fell from first to a month of destruction, and it will be restored to the top.
The blessings of Parshas Balak are blessings transformed from curses, and from Balak himself came Ruth and the seed of Mashiach.
Yiftach, rejected and driven out, represents the 'Tammuz souls' who hold the keys to reopen the gates of the redemption.

belief in and longing for Mashiach
Kohanim, Leviim and the firstborn in the world of tikkun
the months and the twelve shevatim
Yiftach and the keys of the Geulah

title.en: Yerushalayim and the Rambam on Mashiach

summary.en: The Rav speaks of the special merit of learning and davening in Yerushalayim, then opens an uncensored Rambam and translates the beginning of the last chapter of Hilchos Melachim: Mashiach will restore the kingdom of David, and whoever does not await him denies the Torah itself.

title.en: Believing in Mashiach and longing for him

summary.en: The Rav asks how one can be commanded to long for Mashiach, and answers that there is no reason not to: Mashiach brings even material good, so one who is not eager simply does not believe. He shows that the Torah itself, in Nitzavim, promises the ingathering.

title.en: Bilaam's prophecy and the bitter month of Tammuz

summary.en: The Rav reads Bilaam's prophecy of the two Meshichim, David and the final Mashiach. Since Shabbos holds the blessings of the week, Shabbos Balak carries the potential for the three weeks to become days of Mashiach's birth; he then explains why Tammuz is a month of complete strict judgment.

title.en: Korach, machlokes and the Churban

summary.en: Parshas Korach, read at the start of Tammuz, is about machlokes, which destroyed the second Beis HaMikdash through Kamtza and Bar Kamtza. The Rav brings the Midrash that Korach rose again from Gehinnom and the Arizal that he was a tzaddik who argued with good intentions, though he should not have.

title.en: A world that needs tikkun

summary.en: The Rav explains that Adam HaRishon's sin spoiled creation, that every mitzvah repairs and every aveirah spoils, and that the physical pollution of the world mirrors its spiritual state, as in the generation of Noach.

title.en: Why Moshe was not a Kohen; what Korach sought

summary.en: The Rav asks why Moshe Rabbeinu was not a Kohen and brings the Gemara that he lost the Kehunah by refusing to go to Mitzrayim. In the world of tikkun the Leviim will be the Kohanim, as Yechezkel hints, and following the Arizal this is what Korach wanted to bring, not honor for himself.

title.en: Dasan and Aviram and the birthright

summary.en: The Rav asks why Dasan and Aviram of Reuven joined Korach. The avodah originally belonged to the firstborn, the birthright Yaakov and Esav struggled over; the firstborn lost it through the eigel, and Reuven lost his birthright through his sin. Dasan and Aviram wanted the order of the world of tikkun, when the firstborn will serve again.

title.en: Twelve months, twelve shevatim: Tammuz is Reuven

summary.en: From Sefer Yetzirah the Rav explains that each month corresponds to a shevet, and that there are two orders of the shevatim: by birth, on the Choshen, with Reuven first, and by the degalim, with Yehudah first. Tammuz is Reuven's month; as Reuven fell from first to fourth, Tammuz became a month of destruction, and it will be restored to the top.

title.en: Dasan and Aviram: is there no tikkun for them?

summary.en: Dasan and Aviram are behind every quarrel against Moshe Rabbeinu in the Midbar. The Rav brings the Ohr HaChaim that the pasuk of rising from Sheol does not include them, and is troubled: can a Jew be lost forever? He cites the Arizal that even the founder of Christianity has a tikkun, and the Gemara of Onkelos with the Maharal's explanation.

title.en: The Rema MiPano: Dasan and Aviram's tikkun

summary.en: The Rav brings the Rema MiPano's Gilgulei Neshamos that Dasan and Aviram were reincarnated as the two oxen of Eliyahu on Har HaKarmel, a tikkun for refusing to listen to a navi. He gives gematrios linking them to the pasuk of rising from Sheol and to 'HaChodesh Tammuz', so their tikkun means Tammuz will be transformed, as Zechariah says.

title.en: Balak holds the seed of Mashiach

summary.en: Returning to the opening, the Rav shows that Balak, who wanted to drive out Klal Yisrael, carried Mashiach within him through Eglon and Ruth. The blessings of Balak are curses transformed into blessings out of Hashem's love, and Tammuz, he says, has the gematria of Melech HaMashiach.

title.en: Sichon and Og, the locks of Eretz Yisrael

summary.en: In Tammuz Parshas Chukas tells of Moshe's victory over Sichon and Og, whom the Megaleh Amukos calls the locks of Eretz Yisrael. The Rav explains the request for passage as a request to open the locks, and brings Rashi that 'Yisrael sent' and 'Moshe sent' are the same, since the leader is the generation.

title.en: Yiftach reopens the locks

summary.en: In the haftarah, the king of Ammon later denied that the locks were broken and claimed the land; Yiftach, whose name means 'he will open', defeated him. The Rav then tells Yiftach's background: son of a woman of lower standing, driven out by his brothers to Eretz Tov outside Eretz Yisrael.

title.en: Tammuz souls hold the keys of the Geulah

summary.en: Tammuz is the month of exile, yet in it we learn that the gates will be reopened. The Rav explains that rejected souls like Yiftach, not born into the right families, are the 'Tammuz souls' who hold the keys of the Geulah, and that Yiftach's demand to be on top was not ambition but a sign that Tammuz belongs on top.

catalogTitle: ערבה שפילה עולה לגג ארון הקודש

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that Hoshana Rabbah is the day of tefillah, the lowly aravah of Dovid HaMelech, whose prayer completes Moshe Rabbeinu's 516th tefillah, brings down the Beis HaMikdash with its sanctified roof, and rises to the top of the Aron Kodesh.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with Hoshana Rabbah as the peak of Tishrei, when the seventy bulls of Sukkos finish humbling the nations and the war of Gog uMagog is decided. Dovid HaMelech is tefillah itself, and the tasteless, scentless aravah stands for the lowliest Jews, the last generation before Mashiach, whose prayer Hashem does not despise. The front line of the war is the beis medrash and its davening. He then brings the Midrash that Moshe davened 515 tefillos, the Chasam Sofer's question how one learns from an unanswered prayer, and a Belzer teaching that those tefillos built the roof of the heavenly Beis HaMikdash. A long explanation follows of why the roofs of Shiloh and of the first two Batei Mikdash lacked full kedushah: Amalek, whose gematria is ram, blocks it, until Mashiach. The shiur ends with the Ostrovtzer's count of 515 hours from Rosh Hashanah to Shemini Atzeres morning, and the beaten aravah that is placed on the Aron Kodesh.

en: Hoshana Rabbah completes the seventy bulls of Sukkos and is the day of the decisive war of Gog uMagog, a war fought through davening.
Dovid HaMelech is not only someone who davened but tefillah itself, and the aravah, which has neither taste nor smell, is the tefillah of the lowliest Jews.
The front of the war on behalf of Klal Yisrael is not in the halls of governments but in the shuls, in how Jews daven.
Moshe Rabbeinu's 515 tefillos built the roof of the heavenly Beis HaMikdash; the one more tefillah he was stopped from would have brought the Mikdash down below.
The roofs of the first two Batei Mikdash were never sanctified because Amalek, the root of pride, blocks it; when Mashiach erases Amalek the roof will become holy.
From the start of Rosh Hashanah to the last hour before Shemini Atzeres morning there are 515 hours, and the Jews of today will be allowed to daven the missing tefillah until that last hour.
The beaten aravah, like the battered last generation, is placed on the Aron Kodesh and becomes a crown over the Torah of Simchas Torah.

Mashiach and the third Beis HaMikdash

title.en: Hoshana Rabbah, Dovid and the lowly aravah

summary.en: The Rav calls the three days of Hoshana Rabbah, Shemini Atzeres and Simchas Torah the peak of the year, when the seventieth bull ends the subjugation of the nations and Gog uMagog is decided. He explains that Dovid HaMelech is tefillah itself and that the aravah stands for the lowest Jews and the last generation, whose prayer Hashem does not despise.

title.en: The front line is the shul

summary.en: The Rav says the war for Klal Yisrael is fought in the shuls through davening, above all in Pesukei deZimra, Dovid's songs that cut down the kelipos. He compares the hakafos of Sukkos and the seven hakafos of Hoshana Rabbah to the circuits around Yericho, whose fall leads to the building of the walls of Yerushalayim on Shemini Atzeres.

title.en: Taking tefillah from Hoshana Rabbah for the year

summary.en: Each Yom Tov gives a gift for the year, and from Hoshana Rabbah one takes tefillah; the Rav brings a tradition from the Ba'al Shem Tov that davening properly on these three days helps one daven all year. He adds that Eretz Yisrael begs for our tefillos, and brings the Yismach Moshe that on Hoshana Rabbah the nations ask for their share while Dovid HaMelech asks for the geulah.

title.en: Moshe's 515 tefillos and the Chasam Sofer's question

summary.en: The Rav brings the Midrash that Moshe davened 515 tefillos, the gematria of va'eschanan, and that from here one learns to daven in a time of trouble, as the Ramban holds against the Rambam. He then brings the Chasam Sofer's question how one can learn this from an unanswered prayer, and his answer from 'rav lach', which the Rav finds somewhat difficult.

title.en: The heavenly Mikdash built by camps

summary.en: The Rav brings a Belzer teaching: Hashem with His camp built one wall of the heavenly Beis HaMikdash, Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov with their camps the other three, and Moshe the roof with 515 tefillos, five times machaneh. Moshe's tefillos were accepted for the Mikdash above, and one more would have brought it below. He ends asking why Mashiach will stand specifically on the roof of the Mikdash.

title.en: Why Shiloh had a roof of curtains

summary.en: The Rav brings the Gemara that Shiloh had stone walls but a roof of curtains, and asks why. He explains that the roof corresponds to the highest of the ten levels, keser, and only a Mikdash under the gate of heaven in Yerushalayim, aligned with the Mikdash above, could have a roof.

title.en: Amalek and the unsanctified roof

summary.en: The Rav explains 'like the heights' with the Gemara that the upper stories of the Mikdash were not sanctified. Every Mikdash was preceded by a war with Amalek that was never a full victory; Amalek, whose gematria is ram, the root of pride, blocks the sanctity of the roof. Mashiach, called 'rishon', will erase Amalek, and the Mikdash above will come down with a holy roof.

title.en: Humility, kedushah and the third Beis

summary.en: The Rav explains that kedushah rests only where there is bittul to Hashem, while Amalek is pride that pushes away the Shechinah. When Amalek is erased all Jews will be humble, the roof will be sanctified, and the Name and the Throne will be whole. The third Beis is Yaakov's 'bayis', built with the power of the sukkah.

title.en: The child in Lublin and Rabban Gamliel's beracha

summary.en: The Rav tells how Rabbi Shlomo of Lentshna brought his small son to the Lubliner, who was delighted with the child's translation of 'Rabban Gamliel haZaken' as one who thought into his beard. He explains it with the Arizal: Rabban Gamliel's added beracha against the heretics is the only one whose Name carries a kamatz, corresponding to keser, which was needed only after the Churban.

title.en: Moshe joined with Dovid will be Mashiach

summary.en: The Rav brings the Zohar that Shiloh equals Moshe, and the Chasam Sofer that Moshe's soul joined with Dovid's will be Mashiach. In the future a 516th tefillah will be added, bringing the Mikdash above down below. This is the purpose of creation, a dwelling for Hashem in the lowest world, which is why the Tanya says a mitzvah in action outweighs Torah study.

title.en: The sixth camp: Mashiach on the roof

summary.en: The Rav says all of Dovid's tefillos aim at Hashem's glory filling the whole earth, and brings the Kotzker that the earth was given to people to make it heaven. He adds a chiddush: after Hashem, the Avos and Moshe, five camps, Mashiach with his camp will be the sixth, bringing down the Mikdash with a holy roof, when Hashem will be King over all the earth.

title.en: 515 hours to Shemini Atzeres morning

summary.en: The Rav brings the sefer of the Ostrovtzer: the decree can be torn until Hoshana Rabbah and even until Shemini Atzeres morning, and from the start of Rosh Hashanah until then there are 515 hours, one tefillah per hour. Moshe's tefillah was a Hoshana Rabbah tefillah, but he was not allowed to daven in the last hour; today, the Rav says, Jews will be allowed to daven until that last hour.

title.en: The beaten aravah on the Aron Kodesh

summary.en: The Rav brings the Bnei Yissaschar that Hoshana Rabbah is a seal within a seal, and that Jews who have davened for thousands of years are to complete Moshe's 516th tefillah. The aravah, the most common of the minim, is tefillah; like our battered generation it is beaten, and then it is placed on the Aron Kodesh and becomes a crown over the Torah. He closes with wishes for a good psak and the rebuilding of Yerushalayim.

catalogTitle: הוא למעלה מדיבורים ומן הסוכה - מעין עוה"ב - יום מיוחד לישראל

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that Shemini Atzeres is a day above words and above the Sukkah, a taste of the World to Come set aside for Yisroel alone, when a Jew stays with the King Himself instead of taking his gift and going home.

abstract.en: The Rav opens by saying that Shemini Atzeres cannot really be spoken about: it is higher than the Sukkah, a sample of the days of Moshiach, and all the Yomim Tovim are a preparation for it. He tells of a tzaddik who did not answer amen to a blessing for long life because on Shemini Atzeres he was beyond the world. Because the day is so high it needs an intermediate step, the Shabbos-like davening of Hoshana Rabbah. Tefillah belongs to the nations too, but Torah and Shemini Atzeres are for Yisroel alone; the number eight is above nature. With the parable of a king who sends the guests home while his children stay with him, he explains why Shlomo sent the people away on the eighth day. He brings the Sar Shalom of Belz on prayers gathered and accepted on this day, explains that tefillas geshem is a request for Torah, warns that the dancing must be with awe and not frivolity, and closes with the hope that this generation's small turning to Hashem can be the kenishta chada that brings the geulah.

en: Shemini Atzeres is beyond speech and above the Sukkah; it is a sample of the World to Come, and all the Yomim Tovim of the year prepare for it.
A level this high cannot be entered directly; it needs an intermediate step, which is the Shabbos-like davening of Hoshana Rabbah.
Tefillah and the Sukkos offerings include the nations, but Torah and Shemini Atzeres belong to Yisroel alone.
On the eighth day the King sends the guests home with their gifts, but His children, the Jews, want the King Himself and stay with Him.
The rain asked for on Shemini Atzeres has an inner side, which is Torah, and a ben Torah should ask for it with great strength.
The Simchas Torah dancing achieves very much, but only when it is done with seriousness and trembling, not with frivolity or drink.
The service of later, smaller generations is precious, and a small turning to Hashem in this generation can be the kenishta chada that brings the geulah.

parable of the king and his children
dancing with awe on simchas torah

title.en: A day that cannot be spoken about

summary.en: The Rav says Shemini Atzeres is higher than the Sukkah and than speech, a sample of the World to Come; the Chasam Sofer says all the Yomim Tovim prepare for it, which is why it is not called 'chag'. On it one can already point and say 'this is our G-d'.

title.en: The tzaddik beyond the world; davening these days

summary.en: The Rav tells of a great tzaddik who did not answer amen to a blessing for long life, because on Shemini Atzeres he had no connection to the world. He brings the Munkatcher in the name of the Ba'al Shem Tov that one who davens these three days properly will daven so the whole year, and says each person must measure himself so he can daven in the morning with a clear head.

title.en: Hoshana Rabbah as the ladder; the eighth above the world

summary.en: Great things need an intermediate step, and Chol HaMoed is too small to lead into Shemini Atzeres, so Hoshana Rabbah has a Shabbos-like davening. Seven belongs to the world, but the Beis HaMikdash and its inauguration are tied to the eighth; for Jews outside Eretz Yisroel the second day is even greater. He urges everyone to start davening together and to daven aloud, bringing the Ramban.

title.en: Tefillah for all, Torah for Yisroel alone

summary.en: The season so far was tefillah, in which the nations share, but Torah and Simchas Torah are Yisroel's alone. Torah is tied to the eighth, as the Maharal shows from the eighth verse of Tehillim 19. At the hakafos old prayers are raised, and the Ramban says the eighth day is itself the 'hod' that enters the heart.

title.en: The King's children stay with Him

summary.en: Shemini Atzeres is called a 'tosefes', an extra Yom Tov, corresponding to the World to Come. The Rav explains why Shlomo sent the people away on the eighth day with a parable: the guests take the king's gifts and go home, but his children want the king himself, as in 'V'atah Hashem al tirchak'. The same longing is in 'ayeh mekom kevodo' of the Mussaf kedushah.

title.en: The day that includes all; rain as Torah

summary.en: The addition is more than the main part, so Shemini Atzeres includes all the Yomim Tovim; the Komarner's Heichal HaBerachah hints this with a gematria and writes that not everything may be said. The Zohar reads 'great is the day of rain' as Shemini Atzeres; the inner side of rain is Torah, and a ben Torah should daven tefillas geshem with strength for much Torah.

title.en: The Sar Shalom: all the year's prayers rise

summary.en: The Rav brings the Sar Shalom of Belz that on Shemini Atzeres all the prayers of the year that were held back are gathered and accepted, and that the nations conclude their blessings while Jews conclude their judgments. He brings the Zohar that on this day Yisroel are alone with the King, and Reb Pinchas of Koritz that one alone with the King should not ask for trifles.

title.en: Rain of Torah, life, and dancing with awe

summary.en: The Rav explains from the Tanya that the rain is a flow of Torah, unlike the Flood which came because the people refused Torah, and that geshem is said in the blessing of techiyas hameisim, so all service must be with life. Each Jew has an aliyah to the Sefer Torah, which surrounds all Jews in a circle with Hashem in the middle. The dancing must be with awe, as by Rebbe Reb Elimelech where no wine was drunk; he tells of the angel Michael and the torn shoes.

title.en: A clear head, and the kenishta chada

summary.en: The Rav says these three days hold the success of the whole year, and each must measure himself to daven with a clear head, not like 'adam bikar velo yavin' who does not grasp the treasures before him. From the Zohar's kenishta chada he argues that the small turning of our smaller generations is precious, and closes with a tefillah that this Yom Tov bring the geulah.

catalogTitle: The Seed of משיח will Sprout from the Depth of our Times

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that the seed of Mashiach, the Tzemach David, has always grown out of the lowest places, people and times, so that the low generation and the days of Bein HaMetzarim hold Mashiach hidden like a kernel inside the shell of Balak and Moav.

abstract.en: The Rav opens by asking why the sedra is named for Balak and why 'Sdei Moav' in Megillas Rus is spelled with a yud. Following the Imrei Emes, he explains that Yehuda, the king who includes all generations, fell so he could lift up even the lowest generation. From the Ba'al HaTanya he shows that only the earth gives growth, something from nothing, and Mashiach is the Tzemach David that sprouts from the ground. The births of Peretz and of Dovid came about through Tamar and Rus in hidden, seemingly unworthy ways so the Satan would not prosecute. Moav is the forty-ninth, lowest level, and Balak was the shell imprisoning the spark of Mashiach. Using place, soul and time, he shows that the place and the soul of Moav were released, but the time, Bein HaMetzarim, still holds Mashiach. He ends with the generation's task: to break the shell with Torah, tefillah, good middos and chesed.

en: Following the Imrei Emes, the Rav explains that Yehuda, as king of all the generations, fell to the lowest depths so that he could lift up the Jews of the lowest generation.
Only the earth, the lowest element, gives growth, which is creation from nothing; so Mashiach, the Tzemach David, sprouts from the lowest generation.
The lineage of Mashiach passed through Tamar and Rus in circumstances that looked unworthy, so that the Satan would not prosecute against Mashiach's coming.
Moav is the forty-ninth and lowest level, and Balak was the shell imprisoning the spark of Dovid HaMelech hidden in Rus.
In place and in soul the spark of Mashiach was already released from Moav, but in time it is still imprisoned in Tammuz and Av, the days of Bein HaMetzarim.
The Rav says the present era is one long period of Moav and Bein HaMetzarim, and the generation's mission is to break the shell with Torah, tefillah, good middos and chesed.

title.en: Why is the sedra named Balak?

summary.en: The Rav says he will speak in depth, since young people grasp deep ideas, and recalls that he once asked why the sedra is named for Balak when, according to the Gemara, even Nechemia did not merit a sefer called by his name. He announces he will now answer from a different angle.

title.en: Sdei Moav, Yehuda's descent and Dovid's lineage

summary.en: The Rav points out that 'Sdei Moav' in Megillas Rus is mostly spelled with a yud against the rules of grammar, then turns to Yehuda's descent in Parshas Vayeshev. Citing the Imrei Emes, he shows how Dovid HaMelech's lineage passed through low places, from the daughter of Lot through Balak and Eglon to Rus, while Yehuda was always the leader among his brothers.

title.en: The king falls to lift up all generations

summary.en: The Rav explains that Yehuda, as king and head of Klal Yisrael, includes every generation down to the low generation before Mashiach, and he fell by Heaven's design in order to raise those who cannot rise on their own. Dovid HaMelech's teshuvah teaches every individual that he can rise, and the Rav ties Yehuda's descent to the twenty-one mentions of Yovel and the shofar of Mashiach.

title.en: Growth only from the earth: Tzemach David

summary.en: From the Ba'al HaTanya the Rav explains that of the four elements only the lowest, earth, produces growth, which is creation from nothing. The present generation is the lowest, like the earth, and therefore its calling is to bring forth Mashiach, called Tzemach David, a plant that sprouts from the ground.

title.en: Peretz, the Satan, and 'the land I will remember'

summary.en: The Rav explains that Yehuda fell to the ground because Mashiach had to grow from there through Peretz, and that it came about in low circumstances so the Satan would not prosecute. He brings the Zohar that 'the land' remembered together with the Avos is Dovid HaMelech, who was looked down upon, and connects it to Malchus as the last level.

title.en: Tamar and Rus: tznius hidden in descent

summary.en: The Rav compares Rus going down to the goren with Yehuda's fall: both had to happen in hidden ways so the Satan would not catch on. He shows that the Torah and Chazal stress the tznius of both Tamar and Rus, brings that Rus was a gilgul of Tamar, and explains that the Torah itself declares there was no wrongdoing, since they acted to bring Mashiach.

title.en: Forty-nine levels and Arvos Moav

summary.en: The Rav explains that after Malchus shebeMalchus, the forty-ninth day of Sefirah, comes the fiftieth, the shofar of Mashiach. The forty-two journeys in the Midbar were really forty-nine, and the last, Arvos Moav, is the lowest level; Moav itself is forty-nine in gematria. Elimelech went down to Moav to release the spark of Dovid hidden in Rus.

title.en: Balak, the shell around Mashiach

summary.en: The Rav brings the Gemara that through Balak's korbanos he merited that Rus descended from him, and the Rambam that Mashiach comes from Shlomo HaMelech. Balak knew that Mashiach would come from him and, as a klipah like a nut's shell, fought to keep the spark imprisoned. He shows that the letters of Moav spelled out equal 'avdi tzemach' in gematria.

title.en: Place, soul and time: Bein HaMetzarim

summary.en: Citing Sefer Yetzirah, the Rav explains that everything exists in place, time and soul, with Yom Kippur as the example. Mashiach is imprisoned in the place of Moav, in the soul of the daughter of Lot and Rus, and in a time: the days of Bein HaMetzarim, which equal 'Bas Lot' in gematria and which, as Zechariah says, will become days of joy.

title.en: Released in place and soul, not yet in time

summary.en: The Rav explains that the klipah of Moav was broken in place and in soul when Rus emerged, but the klipah of Tammuz and Av is not yet broken, so every year a war is waged against the klipah of Balak. He shows that the passuk forbidding Amoni and Moavi is itself the place where the kernel of Dovid emerges.

title.en: Boaz, Rus and Ploni Almoni

summary.en: The Rav explains that the Oral Torah corresponds to the wife, so a man's chiddushei Torah are hidden in his zivug. The chiddush of 'Moavi and not Moavis' was hidden in Rus, Boaz's zivug, while the closer redeemer refused; Rashi explains he is called 'almoni' because he was a widower of words of Torah, unable to see that chiddush.

title.en: Atika: the yud that hides, the heh that reveals

summary.en: The Rav explains that the point above the yud of Hashem's name is Atika, the level too removed to understand, like the question why Mashiach comes from such a low origin. That is why 'Sdei Moav' is written with a yud while Mashiach is hidden, and with a heh once Rus emerged. Arvos Moav, the forty-ninth stop, lies right across the Yarden, and the present era, full of tumah and nisyonos, is one long period of Moav.

title.en: Shabbos Balak before the Three Weeks

summary.en: The Rav explains that the sedra is called Balak because under that shell lies the kernel of Mashiach, and it is read right before the Three Weeks, when Mashiach struggles to break out like a chick in its egg. He says the Rambam counts this sedra as the first place the Torah speaks of Mashiach, that Tisha B'Av is Dovid's day and Shiva Asar B'Tammuz is Rus's day, and that Balak's korbanos were meant to keep Shiva Asar B'Tammuz imprisoned.

title.en: Our task: break the shell

summary.en: The Rav concludes that great treasures lie hidden in these days, and that this generation, the 'Tisha B'Av of history', is commissioned to break open the klipah of the time of Moav. He says this is done with Torah, tefillah, good middos and chesed, avoiding sinas chinam and reaching out to lift those who have fallen.

catalogTitle: מט' באב עד שמיני עצרת זמן בנין קומת המלכות - זה כנסת ישראל' תורה' וירושלים

oneLiner.en: The Rav explains that from Tisha B'Av until Shemini Atzeres Hashem builds the 'kallah' (Knesses Yisroel, the Torah and Yerushalayim), and that the last, lowliest generation, like the tribe of Dan, is her beauty and is joined to Yehudah on Simchas Torah.

abstract.en: The Rav opens with the verse 'vayiven Hashem Elokim es hatzela', which the seforim read as the building of malchus, the kallah, from Rosh Hashanah to Shemini Atzeres. The kallah is Knesses Yisroel, and also the Torah, Shabbos, Yerushalayim and the esrog. The preparation starts on Tisha B'Av: mourning for Yerushalayim begins its rebuilding, and Sefer Devarim, the seventh book and the kallah, is read from then until Simchas Torah. Like the esrog and like Chavah, Devarim stands apart, and the joy of a wedding is the reuniting of what was separated. Shir Hashirim praises the kallah from the feet upward: the last generation, the 'heel' before Moshiach, is her beauty. Amalek attacks these stragglers, the tribe of Dan, because he envies their future. Shimshon of Dan, whose strength was his hair, prayed 'chazkeini na' for our generation, and on Simchas Torah the end of the Torah is joined to Bereishis, Dan to Yehudah.

en: The building of the kallah, Knesses Yisroel, which is also Yerushalayim, runs from Rosh Hashanah to Shemini Atzeres, and its preparation begins on Tisha B'Av.
Sefer Devarim, the seventh book of the Torah, is the kallah; it is begun on Shabbos Chazon and finished on Simchas Torah, and reading it builds Yerushalayim.
The joy of Shemini Atzeres and Simchas Torah is the joy of a wedding: the reuniting of the kallah, who was separated like the rib from Adam, with the chassan.
Shir Hashirim praises the kallah from the feet upward, because the beauty of Knesses Yisroel is its last, lowliest generation, the heel before Moshiach.
Amalek always attacks the last and weakest, the tribe of Dan, because he envies the future that even the lowest Jew has.
Every Jew of this generation carries a spark of Shimshon, whose task is not to let his 'hair' be shorn, and Shimshon's prayer 'chazkeini na' was composed for us.
On Simchas Torah the end of the Torah, with its forgotten halachos, is joined to Bereishis, and the kallah joins Dan with Yehudah; it is above all the joy of the simple Jew.
